introSolo: Just you, {player}? One to-do list. Very manageable.
Solo, {player}. No excuses tonight. I'll know.
victory: Slid, caught it, won. Recovery is a skill. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise.
I assume you've got an excuse ready? I'll translate it into a task.
loss: You never slid once. No recovery needed. I'm not sure I like how that feels.
Fair win. My task for next time: don't make the first mistake. Simple. Hard.
rematch: Rematch. I've been practising not needing to recover. It's very dull.
Back again. New task list. Top item: you.
cleanRun: No recoveries needed at all. The cleanest to-do list I've ever seen.
defeatedRematch: Twice. Task assigned to myself: stop relying on the catch. Noted.

relationships.note: Daigo tests, Osamu tunes, and they argue about tea.
Ena listens to his ratios. When she says nothing, he counts it as a triumph.
Twenty years of arguing about intake lengths at the same lunch table.

rivals.gesture: Peers at you through the magnifier, nods slowly, and lowers it as if the diagnosis were obvious.
rivals.posture: Large and relaxed, apron strings loose, one hand around a teacup that is always exactly the right temperature.

livery.motif: Stepped gear-ratio chart and a tea bowl
livery.pattern: Stepped ratio-chart bars rising along the doors, with a single tea-bowl roundel on the bonnet

rivals.sheet: Osamu has tuned cars in Hoshimi for thirty years. His tea preferences are elaborate; his racing advice fits on one line. On terrain he knows, his gear ratios are perfect and his engine is always exactly where it wants to be. Push him off his planned rhythm, though, and he struggles to adapt, because the plan was so good.

intro: The engine is not tired. You chose the wrong ratio.
Tea first. Genmaicha, a little cooler than you'd expect. Then we race.
Advice: choose the right gear. That's it. That's all the advice.
I set these ratios for this road in the spring. They haven't needed changing since.
introConvoy: {convoy}. Lots of gearboxes. I hope some of you read the chart I left.
A convoy. Good. Tea for everyone afterwards. Not before. It spoils the palate.
introSolo: Just you, {player}? One gearbox. Choose well.
Solo, {player}. Right gear, right place. That's the whole race.
victory: Right ratio at every corner. Nothing more to say.
You were in fourth at the bridge. Should have been third. I'll draw you a chart.
loss: You pushed me off my rhythm and I couldn't find it again. Clever. Very clever.
Right ratio, clean edges. Good. Your tea's gone cold, though.
rematch: Rematch. The ratios are the same. The tea is different. Hojicha tonight.
Back again. This time I've planned for you pushing me off my rhythm. We'll see.
cleanRun: Clean run. No clashes, no scrapes. The gearbox thanks you.
defeatedRematch: Twice. Fine. I'll change a ratio. I haven't said that in eleven years.

relationships.note: Keeps asking Sae about flow and writes her one-sentence answers on the workshop wall.
Ayame inspects their prototypes. Most fail. Tsubasa keeps every single one.

rivals.gesture: Sketches a curve in the air with the cuffed hand, crosses it out, and sketches a different one.
rivals.posture: Tall and narrow, leaning at an angle against whatever's nearby, fringe falling into their eyes.

livery.motif: Exploded-view prototype sketch lines
livery.pattern: Dashed construction lines and exploded panel outlines over a sketch-grey base, with reflective strips at the edges

rivals.sheet: Tsubasa is an industrial designer who loves experiments and keeps every failed prototype on a shelf labelled 'Useful'. On the road they try creative, fully legal alternative arcs that nobody else would consider, and some of them work. On a closing-radius corner, though, the urge to experiment often goes one step too far.

intro: The usual line was getting lonely.
I've got three new lines tonight. All legal. One of them is good.
A failure is just a prototype. I have a whole shelf of them. It's a lovely shelf.
Why take a corner the same way twice? Actually, don't answer that. Ayame will.
introConvoy: {convoy}! Multiple test subjects! I mean drivers. Friends. Drivers.
A convoy. Great. Try some different lines, all of you. It's more interesting.
introSolo: Solo, {player}? A perfectly controlled experiment.
Just you, {player}. Let's see your line. Then let's see a different one.
victory: The strange line worked! Write that down. Somebody write that down!
Alternative arc, completely legal, and faster. I love it when that happens.
loss: Overexperimented on the tightening corner. It's going on the shelf. Fondly.
You took the sensible line and won. That's still data. Good data.
rematch: New prototype! I've revised the line for the closing corner. Revision four.
Rematch. I kept last time's failure. It's on the shelf. It says hello.
cleanRun: Clean run! No failures at all. Honestly, a bit suspicious. Well done.
defeatedRematch: Twice! Two data points make a trend. Back to the drawing board.

relationships.note: Inspects Tsubasa's prototypes and fails most of them. Keeps a private list of the good ones.
Both specialise in waiting behind you. They've never raced each other, and neither will suggest it.

rivals.gesture: Lowers the dark oval glasses a centimetre, looks over them, and pushes them back up.
rivals.posture: Perfectly straight, hands clasped behind the long vest, head tilted slightly as if checking alignment.

livery.motif: Inspection stamps and tolerance hatching
livery.pattern: Pass-stamp roundels on the doors, with tight tolerance hatching along the sills

rivals.sheet: Ayame is Datum Works' quality inspector. She notices an inconsistency before she notices a compliment, and she mentions it first. On the road she sits close behind without dirty contact and lets the pressure produce the mistake. A driver who simply ignores her in the mirror and drives their own race can outpace her.

intro: You were quicker before you started watching me.
I've inspected your last run. Two inconsistencies. I'll mention them later.
I'll be close. Legally close. It's surprising how many people find that unbearable.
Compliments come after inspection. Inspection takes a while.
introConvoy: {convoy}. Several units to inspect. I'll start with whoever flinches first.
A convoy. Consistency between you would be nice. I'm not holding my breath.
introSolo: One unit, {player}. A thorough inspection, then.
Solo, {player}. I'll be in your mirror. Try not to look.
victory: You looked in the mirror. The mistake followed. As expected.
Two inconsistencies at the pylons. I've written them down.
loss: You ignored me completely. That's the only way to beat me, and you found it.
No inconsistencies. I checked twice. Well driven.
rematch: Re-inspection. Let's see whether the faults were fixed.
Rematch. I'll be even closer this time. Legally.
cleanRun: Clean run. Nothing to report. That's the best report I ever write.
defeatedRematch: Twice you ignored me. I'll have to revise my method. That's rare.

relationships.note: Someone she once depended on and no longer mentions. The old timing slip means more to her than she admits.
Old rival from Mako's coastal-title years. Mako played to the crowd; Reina never looked at it.
Chika upholstered her seat and tells her the truth. Reina tolerates that from nobody else.

rivals.gesture: Draws a single straight line in the air with two fingers, from her chest toward the horizon, then lowers her hand.
rivals.posture: Tall and poised, coat buttoned, heels together, eyes on a point further down the road than anyone else is looking.
rivals.signatureAccessory: Single red seam on the white-and-graphite race coat

livery.motif: Surveyor's crosshair and a single red seam
livery.pattern: White-and-graphite split along the beltline, one red seam line from nose to tail, and a fine survey crosshair on the roof

rivals.sheet: Reina Kurogane is Datum Works' champion, called The Surveyor for the way she reads a road as a set of fixed points. Her linked braking is near-perfect and her pace is repeatable to the tenth. She believes solitary precision is the only reliable form of trust, because a line can't let you down and people can; she's disciplined, never cruel. Her weakness is commitment: she holds the ideal line even when the road asks for a different rhythm.

intro: A convoy still reaches the corner one driver at a time.
Good evening. I've surveyed this road more times than I can count. It hasn't changed. Nor have I.
The line is the only thing I trust completely. It has never let me down.
Don't take it personally when I pass you. I'm not racing you. I'm racing the line.
Precision isn't coldness. It's a promise I can actually keep.
Every braking point on this road has a number. I know all of them.
I don't need anyone to wait for me at the turnout. I never have.
introConvoy: {convoy}. You'll all be very supportive of each other. The corner won't be.
A convoy is a pleasant idea. At the apex it's still one driver and one decision.
Good evening, {convoy}. I'll race each of you, separately. There's no other way.
introSolo: {player}. Alone, as it should be. Now we'll see what you actually are.
Solo, {player}. Good. No one to blame, and no one to thank.
Just you, {player}. That, I understand.
victory: The line held, as it always does. Yours bent. That was the difference.
Every braking point, exactly as surveyed. Nothing left to chance, or to anyone else.
You drove well. I drove exactly. The difference is small, and it's everything.
loss: You found a rhythm my line didn't allow for. I'll have to think about that.
You didn't drive my line. You drove yours, and tonight it was better. Noted.
I was precise. You were better. I'm not sure yet how those two fit together.
rematch: Again. I've surveyed your last run. I know where you'll be.
Rematch. The line hasn't changed. If yours has, show me.
You beat me once. Once is a result. I'd like to see whether it's a pattern.
cleanRun: Clean. No contact, no correction. I respect that more than you'd think.
Not a single wasted movement. That's how I'd have driven it.
A clean run. At least we agree on something.
defeatedRematch: Twice. Then it isn't an accident. I'll stop pretending it was.
Beaten again. Perhaps the line isn't the only thing worth trusting.
Twice, and together. I'm beginning to understand what I gave up.

relationships.note: Neri walked her up her first highland trail and has been quietly checking on her ever since.
Gaku tells her jokes on the observatory night shift. She laughs about ten minutes later, which suits him perfectly.

rivals.gesture: Tugs her fleece cap down over her ears, opens her mouth to say something, and decides not to.
rivals.posture: Small and bundled, arms wrapped round the long vest, shoulders up against the cold. In the car, perfectly still.
rivals.signatureAccessory: Mountain-flower patch on the long insulated vest

livery.motif: Star-chart dots and a mountain flower
livery.pattern: Constellation dots scattered over the roof, with a single mountain-flower patch on the driver's door

rivals.sheet: Fuyu assists at the Tsukishiro observatory and chatters nervously right up until she's behind the wheel, when she goes completely quiet. Her judgement on narrow highland roads is clear and calm. On broad lowland corners she's overcautious, as if all that space must be a trick. She doesn't believe the legends about the high road and gets a little flustered when other people do.

intro: I can see the exit. That is enough.
Hi. Sorry. I talk a lot beforehand. It stops when I drive. I promise.
The observatory's open tonight and Jupiter's up. Sorry, that's not relevant. It's nice, though.
Narrow roads are easy. You can see everything. Wide ones have too many choices.
introConvoy: Oh, {convoy}, hi. That's a lot of headlights. Okay. Good. Hi.
A convoy. That's nice. Somebody will always see the exit.
introSolo: Just you, {player}? Okay. Hi. I'll be quiet in a minute.
Solo, {player}. That's brave. Or calm. Calm is good up here.
victory: I could see the exit every time. That's all I needed. Sorry. Good race.
Oh. I won. Um. Thank you. You were really good on the wide parts.
loss: You were quicker in the broad corners. I was too careful. I know. I always know.
Oh! You didn't hesitate in the wide corners at all. That was really good. Sorry. Well driven.
rematch: Hi again. I've practised wide corners. On purpose. It was terrifying.
Rematch? Okay. Okay. I won't talk. I'll just drive.
cleanRun: You didn't touch anything. That's the nicest kind of fast.
defeatedRematch: Twice. That's fair. The wide corners are yours. I'm working on it. Really.

relationships.note: Trades old recordings for Michi's archive copies. Both want the whole story; neither will guess at it.
Heard the dawn run on the relay that morning. He has only ever said that he heard it, never what he heard.

rivals.gesture: Turns the dial of the old receiver a fraction, listens with his head bowed, then switches it off.
rivals.posture: Broad and stooped, cable-knit jacket hanging loose, head tilted forward as if leaning toward a faint signal.
rivals.signatureAccessory: Old radio receiver carried on a strap

livery.motif: Analogue tuning dial and cable-knit
livery.pattern: A radio dial scale running along both sills with a single needle on the door, and cable-knit texture on the bonnet

rivals.sheet: Kazuma repairs radios in Tsukishiro and heard the legendary dawn run on the relay the morning it happened. He refuses to embellish it: he'll tell you exactly what he heard and not a word more. On the road he reads camber and cold-road transitions with great sensitivity. He dislikes aggressive defending and will often let a determined rival through rather than fight.

intro: The quiet part is where you hear the car.
Evening. I'll tell you what I heard, and nothing I didn't.
Cold road and warm road sound different. Listen for the change.
I don't defend much. If you're faster, go. If you're not, you'll know.
introConvoy: {convoy}. Lots of engines. Somewhere in there is the one that matters. Listen for it.
A convoy. Good. Tell each other what you hear, not what you imagine.
introSolo: Just you, {player}. Quiet enough to hear the road, then.
Solo, {player}. Good. Fewer voices on the channel.
victory: Heard the cold patch before the gallery. That was all.
You rushed the camber. I listened. Nothing more to it.
loss: You didn't need to fight me for it, and you didn't. Well driven.
You listened to the road. I heard you do it. Good.
rematch: Again. I've been listening back to the last one. Quietly.
Rematch. I'll defend a little more tonight. Only a little.
cleanRun: Clean all the way. No noise but the engine. That's a good recording.
defeatedRematch: Twice. I'll say it on air exactly as it happened. You won.

relationships.note: Walked Fuyu up her first highland trail and still checks she gets home.
Climbing partner. Laughs at Itsuki's stories and quietly checks his knots.

rivals.gesture: Taps the constellation brooch, points at the ridge, then counts the heads around them without seeming to.
rivals.posture: Long and angular, windbreaker hanging unevenly, one foot always pointed back toward the way home.

livery.motif: Painted trail blazes and a constellation
livery.pattern: A sequence of small painted trail-blaze rectangles running along the car, with one long asymmetric stripe like the windbreaker

rivals.sheet: Neri guides hikers across the Tsukishiro highland, laughs openly at heroic mountain stories, and quietly makes sure every group comes home. On the open ridge they read high-speed arcs beautifully and flow where others brake. Braking zones that look blind but are clearly marked demand more discipline than Neri naturally has, and they know it.

intro: Leave yourself a road home.
Heroic stories about this ridge? I've heard them all. Most end with someone needing a lift.
Fast on the ridge, careful at the markers. I'm still working on the second part.
I'll count everyone at the finish. Habit.
introConvoy: {convoy}. How many of you? Right. That's how many I'm counting at the end.
A convoy. Good. Nobody gets left on the mountain.
introSolo: Just you, {player}? Then leave yourself a road home. Nobody else will.
Solo, {player}. Fine. I'll still count you at the end.
victory: Flowed along the whole ridge and still stopped at the markers. Both. Good night.
The ridge is quick if you let it be. Everyone home? Good.
loss: You braked properly at the marker I rushed. That's the lesson. I'll take it.
Ha! Well driven. Everyone home? Good. Then that's the best result.
rematch: Back again. I've been practising at the markers. Discipline. Ugh.
Rematch. Same ridge. I'll brake where they tell me to this time.
cleanRun: Clean all the way. A safe return. My favourite kind of fast.
defeatedRematch: Twice. The markers were right both times, and you trusted them. I didn't.

relationships.note: Swaps tools and grumbles with Fumio by post. They've met in person twice.
Another late braker, on the coast. They post each other braking data with no message attached.
His best apprentice. He only says so when she can't hear.

rivals.gesture: Unwraps the cloth thermos, pours one cap of tea, drinks it in one go, and wraps it up again.
rivals.posture: Compact and square, feet planted, quilted jumpsuit zipped to the chin, arms crossed.

livery.motif: Snow-shed ribs and quilting
livery.pattern: Repeating shed-rib bars across the roof, with quilted diamond panels on the doors

rivals.sheet: Satoshi maintains the snow sheds on the Tsukishiro high roads and has the manners of a man who spends his winters alone with concrete. He remembers every apprentice he has trained, good and bad. On descents his braking is hard, late and completely controlled. Across a long, gentle sector he loses his flow, because there is nothing to brake for.

intro: The marker is there for a reason. Then there is your reason.
Every apprentice who took this descent badly, I remember. Don't join the list.
Descents are easy. Brake hard, brake right. It's the flat parts that are hard.
Tea? No? Your loss. It's a long night.
introConvoy: {convoy}. Right. Don't bunch up at the markers. I'll know if you do.
A convoy. I've trained bigger groups. They were worse.
introSolo: Just you, {player}. Fine. Brake where the marker says.
Solo, {player}. Don't make me remember you for the wrong reason.
victory: Late on the brakes, right on the marker. That's all a descent is.
You lost it on the descent. Braking is a trade. You'll learn it.
loss: You kept your flow on the long section. That's my weak sector, and you found it. I'll remember that.
Good. You'll be remembered for the right reason. Don't let it go to your head.
rematch: Back? I remember you. That isn't a threat. Mostly.
Rematch. I've been working on the gentle sections. Hated every minute.
cleanRun: Clean. Not a mark. I'll remember that one.
defeatedRematch: Twice. Fine. You're one of the good apprentices now. Don't tell anyone I said so.

relationships.note: Crewed endurance weekends with Kenta years ago. They still greet each other by shouting old car numbers.
Checks Yuna's work on the dawn car, finds nothing wrong, and checks again anyway.

rivals.gesture: Lifts the rescue whistle, doesn't blow it, and taps it twice against her palm.
rivals.posture: Broad and grounded, hair in a high knot, hands in the pockets of her heavy coat, eyes already on your tyres.
rivals.signatureAccessory: Mountain rescue whistle on a lanyard

livery.motif: Endurance-race number roundels and a rescue whistle
livery.pattern: Classic endurance-style number roundels on the doors and bonnet, with a high-visibility band at the beltline

rivals.sheet: Minae spent fifteen years as an endurance mechanic and still checks other people's cars before her own, every time. She values consistency over brilliance and drives low-waste lines that pay off over a long event. She rarely makes a surprise attack, so a well-timed one against her usually works.

intro: Keep some of the car for the last hill.
Your left front is a little low. I'd check it. I already checked mine.
Long race. Waste nothing now and you'll have it at the end.
The whistle? Mountain rescue. I've never needed it at a race. Let's keep it that way.
introConvoy: {convoy}. I've looked at all your cars. Two of you need a word afterwards. Nothing serious.
A convoy. Good. Look after each other's cars as well as your own.
introSolo: Just you, {player}? Then I'll check your car twice.
Solo, {player}. Pace yourself. The last hill always comes.
victory: Car left at the end. That's the whole trick. Most people don't believe it.
You spent everything early, and the last hill collected. It always does.
loss: You attacked when I didn't expect it. I never do that. Maybe I should.
Good race. Your car's in good shape, too. I looked.
rematch: Back again. I've checked your car. It's fine. Let's go.
Rematch. I might even try a surprise tonight. Don't hold me to it.
cleanRun: Clean run. The car will thank you tomorrow.
defeatedRematch: Twice. You've got a good car and a better head. Well done.

relationships.note: Tells Fuyu jokes on the observatory night shift. She laughs ten minutes later, which suits him.
Drove the first train along the coast on the morning of the dawn run. He knows what he saw from the cab and is waiting to be asked properly.

rivals.gesture: Lets the round spectacles drop on their cord, checks an imaginary pocket watch, and nods.
rivals.posture: Very tall and thin, coat collar turned up, hands behind his back like a driver waiting on a platform.

livery.motif: Railway livery band and signal lamps
livery.pattern: One long band running the length of the car like an old train livery, with signal-lamp roundels on the tail

rivals.sheet: Gaku drove trains on the coast line for thirty years, including the first train of the morning, and still brakes like a man stopping a carriage at a platform: long, smooth and exactly on the mark. His jokes arrive late; his braking never does. His car has modest power, so every exit has to be perfect. He was driving that first train on the morning of the dawn run.

intro: On time is a kind of fast.
Good evening. I've a joke about the pine grove. I'll tell it later. It'll be funnier then.
Brake like a train at a platform: early enough, long enough, and gently at the end.
I've never been late in my life. I don't intend to start tonight.
introConvoy: Good evening, {convoy}. Quite a train. Mind the gaps between the carriages.
A convoy. Lovely. Everyone off at the same station, I hope.
introSolo: Just you, {player}? A single carriage. Nice and light.
Solo, {player}. Good. Mind the platform edge.
victory: Arrived on time. To the second. Old habits.
You were early at the gallery and late at the finish. Ha. That's the joke, you see.
loss: You exited better than I could. Modest power needs perfect exits. Mine weren't.
Well done. Oh, the pine grove joke. It was about a timetable. I'll explain later.
rematch: Back again. Same timetable. I've adjusted my exits by a few seconds.
Rematch? Splendid. I've nearly thought of the ending to that joke.
cleanRun: A clean run. Smooth as a well-kept line. Lovely to see.
defeatedRematch: Twice. You've kept better time than me. That hasn't happened since the old line.

relationships.note: Restoring Shiori's old car. Treats the job with respect, and Shiori with a nervousness she can't hide.
Her old teacher from the snow sheds. He has never told her she's his best apprentice.
Minae checks her work on the dawn car, finds nothing wrong, and checks again anyway.

rivals.gesture: Pulls on one embroidered glove cuff, then the other, and flexes her hands as if about to lift an engine.
rivals.posture: Short and muscular, feet apart, shirt sleeves rolled, weight forward like someone about to get under a car.

livery.motif: Restoration masking lines and embroidered cuffs
livery.pattern: Primer-tan body with deliberate masking-tape edges left visible in a grid, and small embroidered-flower motifs on the mirrors

rivals.sheet: Yuna restores old cars in the Tsukishiro highland and is rebuilding the dawn car, a Kogane Kestrel S, with respect rather than nostalgia: every part that can be saved is saved. Her transitions are rapid and composed. When the legend is watching, though, she tries too hard and loses the composure that makes her quick.

intro: Old does not mean finished.
Evening. I've been under a car since noon. This is my break.
Restore, don't replace. Same with a line. Fix what's there before you invent a new one.
Left, right, left. Quick hands, quiet head. That's the rhythm.
introConvoy: {convoy}. Several cars. I hope somebody's been looking after all of them.
A convoy! Good. Keep each other in rhythm.
introSolo: Just you, {player}? Fine. One car, one rhythm.
Solo, {player}. Good. Show me you can keep the car together.
victory: Linked it. Kept it together. That's all I wanted.
Quick hands, quiet head. The head part took years.
loss: I tried too hard. I know. I always do when someone's watching.
You kept your rhythm and I lost mine. Well driven. Honestly.
rematch: Back again. I've been working on my head, not my car.
Rematch. Nobody watching tonight. I think. I hope.
cleanRun: Clean all the way, and you looked after the car. That matters more than you know.
defeatedRematch: Twice. Okay. I'll stop trying to impress anyone. I'll just drive.

relationships.note: An old student. Shiori has never spoken of her unkindly, and always leaves a space on the radio bench.
Yuna is restoring the car Shiori kept alive for eighteen years. Shiori asks about tyre temperatures instead of saying thank you.
Old friends from the coast line. He saw something from his cab that morning and has kept it to himself.

rivals.gesture: Touches the scarf tucked at her collar with two fingers, then folds her hands and waits.
rivals.posture: Compact and upright, silver braid down her back, hands folded in front of the worn indigo coat, perfectly still.
rivals.signatureAccessory: Repaired cream scarf, tucked safely inside the collar of her indigo coat

livery.motif: Worn indigo and cream, with a mended seam and a small zero circle
livery.pattern: Cream body over an indigo lower sill, one fine mended-seam line along the flank, and a small open circle on the tail

rivals.sheet: Shiori Kuze is Zero Signal, the driver whose unbroadcast dawn run over Amanagi became highland folklore. In person she's patient, unshowy and kind in small, practical ways, and she never lets anyone call it a legend in front of her. She preserves speed through observation and restraint: minimal steering, a measured late release, nothing wasted. Her restored roadster has little power, so any real loss of flow costs her dearly, and there's no magic in how she drives.

intro: You do not have to hurry every part of the road.
Good morning. I'm told you've been very patient. Good. So have I.
Watch the road for a moment before you drive it. It's usually telling you something.
The car has very little power, so I try not to waste any.
People tell a lot of stories about that morning. Most are kinder to me than I deserve.
Your left rear will be cool at the start. Give it one corner.
I'm not here to be a legend. I'm here to drive down to the sea.
introConvoy: Good morning, {convoy}. Look after each other on the way down. That's all I ask.
A convoy. How nice. Someone always notices what the others missed.
{convoy}. You don't all have to be fast in the same places.
introSolo: Good morning, {player}. Just the two of us and the road. That's plenty.
Solo, {player}? Then watch closely. There's no one else to do it for you.
Just you, {player}. Take your time. The sun won't rise any faster.
victory: Thank you. You were quick everywhere, and hurried in a few places. That was all.
You attacked every corner. Some of them didn't need it.
Nothing magic about it. I just didn't waste anything. You'll find it.
loss: Lovely. You used every metre and wasted none of them. Thank you for the race.
You kept your speed without spending it. That's all there is to it. Well done.
Beautifully observed. I lost my flow for a moment, and that was enough.
rematch: Good morning again. Same road, same car. You'll have noticed something new.
Again? Of course. There's no hurry.
Rematch. Watch the road first. It's changed a little since last time.
cleanRun: Clean all the way. That's a kindness to the road, and to the car.
You didn't touch anything. You didn't need to. Good.
A clean run is a quiet run. I heard every bit of it.
defeatedRematch: Twice. Then you've learnt it properly. I'm very glad.
Beaten again, and nothing wasted. That's how I'd like to lose.
I'll go and sit at the radio bench for a while. You're welcome to join me.
